reason: Not that one. Make the move I named.

stop.text: Master Caedan Vale keeps a promise to teach Emrys, son of his former comrade.
You are the spitting image of your father. Seeing you there, I could swear the years had turned back.
Come now, strike the knight, and let me watch how you hold that sword.
What is to be learned from striking a bundle of straw?
Your father asked me the same, boy. A wall is raised one stone at a time.

steps.callout: Blows are traded only in Combat. Declare Combat, and let us begin.

reasons.skip: We came here to train, boy.

steps.callout: Your Power lets you draw a card when you declare Combat. Draw it.

reasons.pick_option: Draw it. You'll often want every card available when entering combat.

bark.text: When you declare, the knight draws three cards to answer with.

steps.callout: Rising Cut is a Strike card, and Strikes hit your opponent's Energy first. The number shown is the Energy this blow will take. Attack with it.

reasons.attack: Start with the Rising Cut, and let the others wait.
reasons.final_strike: You listen about as well as your father did.
reasons.pass: Don't pass with a free swing in front of you. Attack with Rising Cut.

bark.text: Straw and cloth are no match for me!

stop.text: See your Fervor rise? That's the 'Attune' keyword on your Rising Cut taking effect, and at five fervor you climb an Aspect.
Climbing Aspects refills your Energy, and a full Fervor meter while in your last Aspect is one way to win the match.

steps.callout: Attack with the Overhand Cut, and watch what happens when we strike an opponent with no Energy to cushion the blow.

reasons.attack: Attack with the Overhand Cut while the knight stands open.
reasons.final_strike: Not yet. A Final Strike ends your attacks, and you still hold good cards.
reasons.pass: Keep at it, boy. The knight has no Energy left.

stop.text: Its Energy was spent, so your Overhand Cut cost its Life Deck a card for every wound. Emptying that deck is another way you can win.

steps.callout: Now let's try an Art, which is different from a Strike. By default an Art costs 2 Energy to perform, but deals Wound damage directly to the Life Deck. Attack with it now.

reasons.final_strike: Not yet. A Final Strike would end your attacks with the Dagger still in your hand.
reasons.pass: One more before you rest. Attack with the Thrown Dagger.

bark.text: Your physical Might is linked with your Energy, so paying for the Dagger weakened your Strikes.

steps.callout: Your Parry only defends, so you're out of attacks. Pass.

reasons.final_strike: Keep the Parry, you'll need it soon.

stop.text: Well struck, boy, but now it's time to test your defense.
Against this thing?
Caedan ties a rope to the Straw Knight's arm.
The opponent's power is a Strike, so keep a guard ready.

bark.text: This time the knight declared, so you're the defender, and you draw three cards to answer with.

steps.callout: Your Parry stops Strikes, and a stopped attack does no damage. Defend with the Parry.

reasons.no_defense: Defend. The Parry stops this Strike.

steps.callout: Combat is an exchange, so after you defend, the swing is yours. Attack with the Rising Cut.

reasons.pass: Hit it back while you can.

steps.callout: A Final Strike discards any card, even a Parry, for a plain Strike, but then you sit out this Combat. Make one.

reasons.pass: Swing. A pass gives up your attack.

steps.callout: Catch your breath. A turn without Combat lets you Recover a card at its end. Skip Combat.

reasons.declare: Not this turn. Skip, and you can recover a card.

steps.callout: Before a turn ends, both sides discard down to one card. Keep the Parry, since your opponent attacks next.

reasons.keep: Keep the Parry. You'll be the one defending next.
reasons.discard_all: Keep one. It carries over to the next turn.

steps.callout: Recover puts your top discard under your Life Deck, one more wound you can take. Recover a card.

reasons.no_recover: Recover it. That's one card of life back.

stop.text: Good. It is time for a proper opponent.
Caedan draws his sword.
Finally!
Keep your guard up.

bark.text: Read a rival's Power. Mine just took a Sword card from my top eight.

steps.callout: Attack with the Rising Cut.

bark.text: I stopped it, but your Attune still counted. Only Hit text needs the blow to land.

steps.callout: My Riposte stopped your Cut and lets me swing it back at you. Defend with your Parry.

reasons.no_defense: Defend. You kept the Parry for this.

steps.callout: Strike cards can't stop Emrys Risks It All, and my Riposte is one. Attack with it.

reasons.attack: Risk it. My Riposte can't stop that one.

bark.text: Every Strike that lands drains your Energy, and your Might with it.

steps.callout: Its Attune brings your Fervor to five. Attack with the Rising Cut.

stop.text: Grey metal dragon scales close over Emrys' forearms.
Master Vale... my arms?
The ironblood. We will have to let your father know.
Is it... good?!
It saw him through many fights in the war.
If you learn to harness it, it will serve you well.
You've climbed an Aspect. Your Energy is full and your Fervor resets to zero.
Aspect changes can provide benefits like higher Might values, Energy surge rates, Powers, and more.
Again.
Let us see what your newfound power can do. Show me.

steps.callout: A Drill is a Non-Combat card, which can not be played during Combat. This one adds a passive +2 to your Strikes while on the field. Play it now.

reasons.place: Place the Clawed Hands Drill first.
reasons.done: Not yet. Place your Drills first.

steps.callout: This Drill is a Defense Shield, so it stops my first Strike to get through each Combat. Place the Hardscale Drill.

reasons.done: Not yet. The Hardscale Drill goes out too.

steps.callout: Your Drills are set, but one card makes for a poor Combat. Skip it and Recover for now. When I attack, you'll draw three.

reasons.declare: Not with one card in hand. Skip, and Recover.

steps.callout: Good, a deep breath in and hold it. Steady yourself for what is to come.

reasons.no_recover: Recover it. That's one card of life back.

steps.callout: Your new Power searches your Life Deck whenever you enter Combat. The Ironscale Hide stops any attack, so pick it.
Your Hardscale Drill stops my first Strike each Combat, so keep your cards. Take it.

reasons.defend: Save your cards. The Drill has this one.

bark.text: Woah, I didn't feel a thing!

steps.callout: The Lashing Tail deals wounds as well as Energy, and your Drill adds 2. Attack with it.
My Declaration is an Art, and your Parries stop only Strikes. The Hide stops any attack, so defend with it.

reasons.no_defense: Defend. Only your Hide can stop an Art.

bark.text: My shout carried Disrupt 2. It knocks your Fervor down and slows your climb.

steps.callout: You have no attacks in hand, but using a Final Attack would prevent you from defending my remaining attacks. Pass for now.
My Sword Draw is a Strike, so a Parry stops it. Your defense shield is spent, so defend with a Parry now.

reasons.no_defense: Defend. A Parry stops a Strike.

steps.callout: You still have no attacks. Pass again.

says.text: Parries can't stop an Art and your Hide is spent, so you have no choice but to take this attack.

steps.callout:
Some cards have Endurance, which soaks extra wounds when the card is flipped. 
 This one has Endurance 4, so you may remove it from the game instead to soak 4 additional wounds. Use Endurance now.

reasons.no_endure: Use it. You lose four cards instead of eight.

steps.callout: Pass, and let us call this bout.

stop.text: You are taking to your new abilities quite naturally. Well done, Emrys.
*panting* Thank you, Master Vale!
Rest now. That will do for today.
One more bout, please! I've only just found my feet!

bark.text: Caedan sighs, and raises his sword once more.

stop.text: Very well, one more. Your form is still sloppy, but you fight with conviction.
With training, you may surpass even your father.

steps.callout: You hold a full hand this time, and are well positioned for an attack. Declare Combat.

reasons.skip: Not this time. Your hand is full.

steps.callout: Your Power fetches a card as you enter Combat. Pick the Routing Roar, an Art to finish with.

reasons.pick_none: Pick the Routing Roar. It ends this.

steps.callout: Open with your Overhand Cut. It is a Strike, so your Clawed Hands Drill adds 2 to it.

reasons.attack: The sword first. Attack with the Overhand Cut.

steps.callout: Your Hardscale stops my first Strike in this Combat too. Take it.

reasons.defend: Save your Parry. The Drill has this one.

bark.text: I could get use to these scales!

steps.callout: Empower adds extra wounds but drops the text after the keyword. Since this hits Allies, and I have none, you can attack with the Empowered variant with no loss.

reasons.attack: Empower it. Its text hits Allies, and I have none.

steps.callout: Five or more wounds in one attack make a critical hit. Choose Disrupt 1 to slow my climb.

reasons.no_critical: Don't waste it. Disrupt 1 slows my climb.

stop.text: First Plate is your last Aspect here, so the next time your Fervor fills, you win the duel.
But enough. Let's go show your father those arms.
Same time tomorrow, Master Vale?
...Same time tomorrow.
